## Authenticity

The scenes early in the film of Ralston's encounter with the two hikers were altered to portray Ralston showing them a hidden pool, when in reality he just showed them some basic climbing moves. Despite these changes, with which he was initially uncomfortable, Ralston says the rest of the film is "so factually accurate it is as close to a documentary as you can get and still be a drama."[[6]](127_Hours#cite_note-6)

Other changes from the book include omissions of descriptions of Ralston's efforts after freeing himself: his bike was chained to itself, not to the tree as depicted at the beginning of the movie; he had to decide where to seek the fastest medical attention; he took a photo of himself at the small brown pool from which he really did drink; he had his first bowel movement of the week; he abandoned many of the items he had kept throughout his confinement; he got lost in a side canyon; and he met a family from the <Netherlands> (not an American family), Eric, Monique, and Andy Meijer, who already knew that he was probably lost in the area, thanks to the searches of his parents and the authorities. (The actor who plays Eric Meijer, [Pieter Jan Brugge](Pieter_Jan_Brugge "Pieter Jan Brugge"), is Dutch.)

Franco is never shown uttering even an "Ow"; Ralston wrote that this is accurate.[[7]](127_Hours#cite_note-7) Ralston did send Monique and Andy to run ahead to get help, and Ralston did walk seven miles before the helicopter came,[[8]](127_Hours#cite_note-8) although this trek is shown in the film's alternative ending.

## Production

[Danny Boyle](Danny_Boyle "Danny Boyle") had been wanting to make a film about Ralston's ordeal for four years;[[9]](127_Hours#cite_note-indieWire-9) he wrote a [film treatment](Film_treatment "Film treatment") and Simon Beaufoy wrote the screenplay.[[10]](127_Hours#cite_note-Variety-10) Boyle describes *127 Hours* as "an action movie with a guy who can't move."[[11]](127_Hours#cite_note-11) He also expressed an interest for a more intimate film than his previous film, *[Slumdog Millionaire](Slumdog_Millionaire "Slumdog Millionaire")* (2008): "I remember thinking, I must do a film where I follow an actor the way [Darren Aronofsky](Darren_Aronofsky "Darren Aronofsky") did with *[The Wrestler](The_Wrestler_(2008_film) "The Wrestler (2008 film)").* So *127 Hours* is my version of that."[[12]](127_Hours#cite_note-12)

Boyle and [Fox Searchlight](Fox_Searchlight "Fox Searchlight") announced plans to create *127 Hours* in November 2009.[[13]](127_Hours#cite_note-13) [Cillian Murphy](Cillian_Murphy "Cillian Murphy") was reportedly approached by Boyle to play Ralston.[[14]](127_Hours#cite_note-14) In January 2010, [James Franco](James_Franco "James Franco") was cast as Ralston.[[15]](127_Hours#cite_note-Franco-15) In March 2010, filming began in Utah;[[16]](127_Hours#cite_note-16) Boyle intended to shoot the first part of the film with no dialogue.[[9]](127_Hours#cite_note-indieWire-9) By 17 June 2010, the film was in post-production.[[17]](127_Hours#cite_note-17)

Boyle made the very unusual move of hiring two cinematographers to work first unit, [Anthony Dod Mantle](Anthony_Dod_Mantle "Anthony Dod Mantle") and [Enrique Chediak](Enrique_Chediak "Enrique Chediak"), each of whom shot 50 percent of the film by trading off with each other. This allowed Boyle and Franco to work long days without wearing out the crew.[[18]](127_Hours#cite_note-18)

Boyle enlisted makeup effects designer [Tony Gardner](Tony_Gardner_(designer) "Tony Gardner (designer)") and his effects company, [Alterian, Inc.](Alterian%2C_Inc. "Alterian, Inc."), to re-create the character's amputation of his own arm. Boyle stressed that the realism of the arm as well as the process itself were key to the audience's investing in the character's experience, and that the makeup effects' success would impact the film's success.
